chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about a man who sells to another man food in bulk (akrar), and he does not have what is needed to complete what he sold, so he says to him: Take from me, in place of every qafiz of wheat, two qafizs of barley, until he receives the full measure of what was lacking in the volume.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid, because the origin of the barley is from the wheat, but he should refund him from the dirhams according to the amount lacking in the measure.'

key_terms.قَفِيزٍ: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method to compensate for a shortage in bulk food sales according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that substituting wheat with barley in a fixed ratio constitutes *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange of same genus) because barley is fundamentally derived from the same category as wheat, thereby invalidating the barter. This ruling emphasizes the necessity of monetary compensation for the shortfall to preserve the integrity of the contract, a principle central to Shia jurisprudence on *bay' al-mu'atah*. The distinction highlights the scholarly focus on preventing hidden interest in commodity trades where quality or quantity disparities exist within the same genus.
